questions.question: How many Flex Alerts did the California ISO call in 2022?
questions.answer: The California ISO called 11 Flex Alerts in 2022, counting one record per Flex Alert day (caiso_grid_emergencies, event_type flex_alert). The count covers 2022-01-01 to 2023-01-01 in Pacific time. Three were in August: 16, 30 and 31 August. Eight were in September, one on each day from 1 to 8 September. The table is a source table and is public.

questions.question: How many real-time settlement intervals at ERCOT's West hub (HB_WEST) had a negative price in 2025?
questions.answer: HB_WEST had 2,724 real-time 15-minute settlement intervals with a price at or below zero in 2025 (ercot_peak_premium_annual, variable n_negative). That count is out of 35,040 intervals, so the year is complete. Two caveats apply. The table defines n_negative as intervals <= 0 USD/MWh, so it may include some intervals priced at exactly zero. Also, the year is the ERCOT operating year in Central time. The table is derived by the ERW from ERCOT real-time prices.

questions.question: On the generator page's rule, how much margin over fuel did a gas peaker at ERCOT's hub average earn in August 2026, in USD per MW?
questions.answer: A gas peaker at ERCOT's HB_HUBAVG earned 6,645.07 USD/MW in August 2026 (merchant_revenue_monthly, variable peaker_revenue_per_mw, derived table). The month is complete: peaker_hours is 744 and hours_in_month is 744. I read peaker_revenue_per_mw as the generator page's margin over fuel. The same table's gross peaker_sales_per_mw is higher, at 14,199.85 USD/MW. The table's method note was not available to confirm that reading. Times are UTC month starts, which here match the local August.

questions.question: How much solar generation did the California ISO curtail in September 2026, in MWh?
questions.answer: CAISO curtailed 163,494.642 MWh of solar in September 2026. This is the sum of 30 daily rows (1-30 September) in caiso_curtailment_daily, a source table. Its day boundaries are CAISO's, which I did not check. All 30 days are held. The derived monthly table iso_curtailment_monthly gives the same figure, 163,494.642 MWh. I read the daily table's dates as calendar dates, so no time-zone conversion was applied.

questions.question: Measured as its demand less its own generation (the balance), how much electricity did the California ISO import on net in August 2026, in MWh?
questions.answer: On the balance measure (demand less the BA's own net generation), the California ISO (EIA-930 balancing authority CISO) imported 4,981,715 MWh on net in August 2026 (ba_supply_monthly, variable net_import_balance_mwh, derived table). The row covers all 31 of 31 days, with none left out, and equals 19.66 pct of demand. Times are the table's UTC months. The ERW notes that from December 2025 CAISO's balance reads about 10 points higher than its flows. This is because EIA's published net generation for CAISO dropped then. Summing the interchange flows between pairs of balancing authorities gives a lower figure, 2,101,695 MWh (net_import_pairs_mwh, same table).

questions.question: For ERCOT projects that reached operation in 2024, what was the median time from interconnection request to operation, in months?
questions.answer: The median time from interconnection request to operation for ERCOT projects that reached operation in 2024 was 43.5 months. The summary table (interconnection_durations_summary, derived from Berkeley Lab's Queued Up file) gives this as median_months, with 95 projects (projects) and an interquartile range of 28.25 to 55.75 months. The project-level table (interconnection_durations) gives the same median over 95 ERCOT projects with operation_year 2024.

questions.question: In Berkeley Lab's queue data, of the capacity that entered ERCOT's interconnection queue in 2019, how many MW are now operating?
questions.answer: In Berkeley Lab's Queued Up 2026 edition (lbnl_interconnection_queue, requests through 2025), 9,451.88 MW of the capacity that entered ERCOT's queue in 2019 now has status "operating". That is the sum of capacity_mw over 64 projects with queue year 2019 in the ERCOT region. The other 2019 ERCOT entries are 11,592.93 MW active, 1,825.15 MW suspended and 20,687.75 MW withdrawn. Together the four statuses come to 43,557.71 MW across 245 projects.

questions.question: How many MW of conventional steam coal generators retired in 2025, in the warehouse's table of retired generators?
questions.answer: In 2025, 2,626 MW of Conventional Steam Coal generators retired. This is the sum of nameplate_mw over 8 generators in eia860m_retired_generators (EIA-860M, vintage 2026-09), filtered on retirement date in 2025. The retirements fell in five months: February (445.5 MW), March (425.9 MW), October (920 MW), November (820 MW) and December (14.6 MW). The table holds no Conventional Steam Coal retirements dated 2026.
